critique.evidence: The screen directly supports the intent-integrity story by contrasting human-visible commerce content with agent-retrieved context, naming zero-width characters and invisible CSS, and preserving a read-only merchant artifact. However, every screenshot shows Human Vision with the reveal toggle off, so there is no visible injected instruction, provenance trail, resulting intent conflict, or demonstrated defensive decision. The wallet-voucher and mandate framing is commerce-relevant, but no explicit Mastercard use case or payment-control consequence is evidenced.
critique.fix: Show the toggled Agent Vision state in the demo: expose a safely truncated, watermarked injected instruction beside its DOM/retrieval provenance, identify the trusted user mandate it conflicts with, and show the resulting block/escalation before a payment or mandate change. Tie that decision explicitly to a Mastercard-relevant checkout, wallet, or merchant-risk workflow.
